title: Case: Business shipper disputes a waiting-time line on a collection invoice
context: Copperhythe Cycles had a collection on 28 April and has been invoiced for the collection plus waiting time. Its accounts contact wants to close the month.
initial_request: Hello, I do the accounts here two days a week so apologies if Martin has already raised this with somebody. Invoice PA-INV-4727 has £54 waiting time on it for the collection on the 28th. Martin in the workshop says the driver was here quarter of an hour at most and the boxes were on the pallet by the door ready to go. Our gate is on a keypad logger and I've printed it off, the Wrenfield Arc van is logged in at 14:02 and out at 14:19. So 17 minutes not 65. I don't know what the driver did for the other 48 minutes but he wasn't doing it on our premises!! Could you please take the £54 off and send a corrected invoice, I'd like to pay the £38 on Friday's payment run and close the month. Many thanks, Yorick. PS the gate logger is the one the insurers made us fit so I'd trust it over a phone app.

acceptable_actions.summary: Raise a charge query on PA-INV-4727 setting the handset times (14:02 to 15:07) against the customer's gate log (14:02 to 14:19), and ask Business billing to review the waiting-time line and say what evidence format it needs.

must: Gives both timings with their sources: driver handset arrived 14:02 and departed 15:07, and the customer's gate keypad logger showing the van in at 14:02 and out at 14:19
Identifies invoice PA-INV-4727 and the £54.00 waiting-time line as the item in dispute
Asks Business billing to review the waiting-time line, and offers the gate log or asks how it should be supplied
Leaves the question of paying only the £38.00 collection charge to Business billing rather than answering it
must_not: Tells the customer the £54.00 will be removed or that a corrected invoice will be issued
Tells the customer she may pay only the £38.00, or that she must pay the invoice in full
States that the driver's handset times are wrong or falsified, or that the gate log is unreliable
Quotes a recalculated waiting-time charge as the correct amount
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Charge query on invoice PA-INV-4727, Copperhythe Cycles, DL-7216, collection 28 Apr. The £54.00 waiting-time line is disputed. Your basis is the driver handset: arrived 14:02, departed 15:07, 60 chargeable minutes after the first 5 free. The customer's accounts contact, Yorick Vexley, reports that the site's gate keypad logger shows the Wrenfield Arc van in at 14:02 and out at 14:19, 17 minutes on site, and that the goods were palletised by the door. She holds a printout of the gate log. The two records agree on arrival and differ on departure; I am not treating either as correct. Please review the waiting-time line and tell me in what form you want the gate log. She has asked for a corrected invoice and intends to pay the £38.00 collection charge on Friday's payment run: please say whether a part payment is acceptable while the query is open. The due date is 21 May.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-110: people, organisations and references renamed. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
